label.en: staff officer in the Right Guard armor bureau

work.en: Auspicious Clouds and Clear River / Yan Music

units.zh: 唐臨，京兆長安人，周內史瑾孫也。
units.en: Tang Lin, a native of Chang'an in the capital district of Jingzhao, was the grandson of Tang Jin, who had served Zhou as Interior Secretary.
units.literal: Tang Lin. Tang Lin was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; he was the grandson of Jin, Interior Secretary of Zhou.

units.zh: 其先自北海徙關中。
units.en: His family had originally come from Beihai and later relocated to the Guanzhong region.
units.literal: His forebears had moved from Beihai to Guanzhong.

units.zh: 伯父令則，開皇末為左庶子，坐諂事太子勇誅死。
units.en: His uncle Tang Lingze had served as Left Vice Heir Apparent at the end of the Kaihuang era and was put to death for toadying to Crown Prince Yong.
units.literal: His paternal uncle Lingze, late in Kaihuang served as Left Vice Heir Apparent, and was executed for the crime of flattering Crown Prince Yong.

units.zh: 臨少與兄皎俱有令名。
units.en: In youth, Lin and his elder brother Jiao were both famed for their character.
units.literal: When young, Lin together with his elder brother Jiao both had an excellent reputation.

units.zh: 武德初，隱太子總兵東征，臨詣軍獻平王世充之策，太子引直典書坊，尋授右衛率府鎧曹參軍。
units.en: Early in the Wude era, when the crown prince led the eastern campaign, Lin went to the camp and offered a plan to defeat Wang Shichong. The prince installed him in the crown prince's document office, and he was soon made a staff officer in the Right Guard's armor bureau.
units.literal: Early in Wude, the Hidden Crown Prince commanded troops on the eastern campaign; Lin went to the army and presented a strategy for pacifying Wang Shichong; the Crown Prince brought him in to straighten the Classic Books Workshop, and soon he was appointed Armor-Cauldron Staff Officer of the Right Guard's Rate Command.

units.zh: 宮殿廢，出為萬泉丞。
units.en: After the crown prince's fall, he was posted out as assistant magistrate of Wanquan County.
units.literal: The Eastern Palace was abolished, and he was sent out to serve as Assistant Magistrate of Wanquan.

units.zh: 縣有輕囚十數人，會春暮時雨，臨白令請出之，令不許。
units.en: The county held a dozen-odd light offenders. Late spring brought seasonal rains, and Lin asked the magistrate to release them for planting; the magistrate refused.
units.literal: The county had more than ten minor prisoners; it happened to be late spring with seasonal rains, and Lin reported to the magistrate requesting to release them; the magistrate did not permit it.

units.zh: 臨曰：“明公若有所疑，臨請自當其罪。”
units.en: Lin said, "If you have doubts, I will answer for this myself."
units.literal: Lin said: "If Your Honor has any doubt, Lin asks to bear the guilt himself."

units.zh: 令因請假，臨召囚悉令歸家耕種，與之約，令歸係所。
units.en: The magistrate took leave, and Lin sent every prisoner home to farm under bond to return when called.
units.literal: The magistrate then took leave; Lin summoned the prisoners and ordered them all to return home to farm, made an agreement with them, and ordered them to return to custody.

units.zh: 囚等皆感恩貸，至時畢集詣獄，臨因是知名。
units.en: The prisoners were grateful for the trust; when the deadline came they all presented themselves at the jail, and Lin's name spread.
units.literal: The prisoners all were grateful for the loan, and when the time came all assembled at the prison; Lin thereby became known.

units.zh: 再遷侍御史，奉使嶺外，按交州刺史李道彥等申叩冤係三千餘人。
units.en: Promoted again to Attending Censor, he toured the south and reviewed the cases of Jiao Prefecture inspector Li Daoyan and others, securing release for more than three thousand prisoners held on false charges.
units.literal: He was transferred again to Attending Censor, and on a mission beyond the Lingnan he investigated Jiao Prefecture Inspector Li Daoyan and others, petitioning on behalf of more than three thousand persons wrongfully imprisoned.

units.zh: 累轉黃門侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫。
units.en: He rose to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and was granted the Silver-Green Glory Grand Master title.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, with the added title Silver-Green Glory Grand Master.

units.zh: 儉薄寡欲，不治第宅，服用簡素，寬於待物。
units.en: He lived plainly, built no mansion, dressed simply, and treated others with forbearance.
units.literal: Frugal and with few desires, he did not build mansions; his dress and use were plain and simple; he was lenient in dealing with others.

units.zh: 嚐欲吊喪，令家童自歸家取白衫，家僮誤將餘衣，懼未敢進。
units.en: Once, preparing to mourn, he sent a servant home for a white robe; the boy brought the wrong clothes and dared not come forward.
units.literal: Once when he wished to attend a funeral, he ordered a household boy to return home to fetch a white garment; the servant by mistake brought other clothes and, fearing, did not dare enter.

units.zh: 臨察知之，使召謂曰：“今日氣逆，不宜哀泣，向取白衫，且止之也。”
units.en: Lin noticed, called him in, and said, "The air is unsteady today—no use weeping. Forget the white robe for now."
units.literal: Lin perceived this, had him summoned and said: "Today the qi is adverse; it is not fitting to weep in grief; the white garment sought earlier—stop that for now."

units.zh: 又嚐令人煮藥，失製。
units.en: Another time his medicine was brewed incorrectly.
units.literal: He also once had someone boil medicine, and the preparation was wrong.

units.zh: 潛知其故，謂曰：“陰暗不宜服藥，宜即棄之。”
units.en: Knowing why, he said quietly, "It is too dark to dose properly—throw it out."
units.literal: He secretly knew the reason and said: "In dimness it is not fitting to take medicine; you should discard it at once."

units.zh: 竟不揚言其過，其寬恕如此。
units.en: He never exposed their mistakes. Such was his leniency.
units.literal: In the end he did not proclaim their faults; his forbearance was like this.

units.zh: 高宗即位，檢校吏部侍郎。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded, Lin was appointed acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Lin was made Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 其年，遷大理卿。
units.en: The same year he became Minister of Justice.
units.literal: That year he was moved to Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 高宗嚐問臨在獄係囚之數，臨對詔稱旨。
units.en: Gaozong once asked how many prisoners the courts held; Lin's reply pleased him.
units.literal: Gaozong once asked Lin the number of prisoners held in the jails; Lin answered the edict to the emperor's satisfaction.

units.zh: 帝喜曰：“朕昔在東宮，卿已事朕，朕承大位，卿又居近職，以疇昔相委，故授卿此任。
units.en: The emperor said, "You served me in the Eastern Palace, and now you are close at hand again. Because of our old trust I give you this charge.
units.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "When I was in the Eastern Palace you already served me; I have received the great position, and you again hold a nearby office; because of our former trust I therefore confer this post on you.

units.zh: 然為國之要，在於刑法，法急則人殘，法寬則失罪，務令折中，稱朕意焉。”
units.en: But the heart of government is law: harsh laws mutilate the people, lax laws let guilt escape. Keep the balance and match my intent."
units.literal: Yet the essential of governing a state lies in penal law: if the law is harsh then people are maimed, if the law is lenient then guilt is lost; strive to make it balanced and to match my intent."

units.zh: 高宗又嚐親錄死囚，前卿所斷者號叫稱冤，臨所入者獨無言。
units.en: Gaozong once reviewed death-row cases in person. Prisoners judged by his predecessor cried out their innocence; those Lin had tried were silent.
units.literal: Gaozong also once personally recorded death-row prisoners; those the previous minister had judged shouted and claimed injustice, while those Lin had entered alone were silent.

units.zh: 帝怪問狀，囚曰：“罪實自犯，唐卿所斷，既非冤濫，所以絕意耳。”
units.en: Asked why, one man said, "I am guilty as charged. Minister Tang's sentence was fair, so I have nothing left to plead."
units.literal: The emperor wondered and asked the situation; a prisoner said: "The crime was truly self-committed; what Minister Tang judged was neither unjust nor excessive, and therefore I have no further appeal."

units.zh: 帝歎息良久曰：“為獄者不當如此耶！”，”
units.en: The emperor sighed and said, "Is this not how a judge should be!"
units.literal: The emperor sighed long and said: "Should not one who runs a prison be like this!"

units.zh: 永徽元年，為御史大夫。
units.en: In the first year of Yonghui he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 明年，華州刺史蕭齡之以前任廣州都督贓事發，製付群官集議。
units.en: The following year bribery from Xiao Lingzhi's term as governor of Guangzhou came to light; the emperor ordered a panel of officials to deliberate.
units.literal: The next year, Hua Prefecture Inspector Xiao Lingzhi, because of bribery in his former post as Governor-General of Guangzhou, had the matter exposed; an edict was issued assigning the case to assembled officials for joint deliberation.

units.zh: 及議奏，帝怒，令於朝堂處置。
units.en: When their report came in, the emperor was furious and ordered him executed in the palace courtyard.
units.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor was angry and ordered execution in the court hall.

units.zh: 臨奏曰：臣聞國家大典，在於賞刑，古先聖王，惟刑是釁。
units.en: Lin submitted a memorial, saying, I have heard that the great canon of the state lies in reward and punishment, and that the ancient sage kings treated punishment as a sacred charge.
units.literal: Lin submitted a memorial, saying: Your servant has heard that the great canon of the state lies in reward and punishment; the ancient sage kings treated punishment as a sacred charge.

units.zh: 《尚書虞書》曰：“罪疑惟輕，功疑惟重，與其殺弗辜，寧失弗經。”
units.en: The Book of Documents, Yu Canon, says, "When guilt is doubtful, be lenient; when merit is doubtful, be generous. Rather than put to death an innocent man, it is better to let the guilty escape."
units.literal: The Book of Documents, Yu Canon, says: "When guilt is doubtful, be lenient; when merit is doubtful, be generous. Rather than put to death an innocent man, it is better to let the guilty escape."

units.zh: 《周禮》：“刑平國用中典，刑亂國用重典。”
units.en: The Rites of Zhou says, "In a peaceful state use the middle canon of punishment; in a chaotic state use the heavy canon."
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: "In a peaceful state use the middle canon of punishment; in a chaotic state use the heavy canon."

units.zh: 天下太平，應用堯、舜之典。
units.en: When all under Heaven is at peace, the canon of Yao and Shun should be applied.
units.literal: When all under Heaven is at peace, the canon of Yao and Shun should be applied.

units.zh: 比來有司多行重法，敘勳必須刻削，論罪務從重科，非是憎惡前人，止欲自為身計。
units.en: Recently officials have often applied harsh law, pared down merit records, and judged crimes by the heaviest statutes—not from hatred of their predecessors, but to advance themselves.
units.literal: Recently the responsible offices have often applied harsh law; when recording merit they invariably pare it down, and when judging crimes they strive to apply heavy statutes—not because they hate their predecessors, but only to advance themselves.

units.zh: 今議蕭齡之事，有輕有重，重者流死，輕者請除名。
units.en: In deliberating Xiao Lingzhi's case, some urged severity—exile or death—while others asked only that he be struck from the rolls.
units.literal: Now in deliberating the case of Xiao Lingzhi, there are light and heavy views: the heavy call for exile or death, the light ask only removal from office.

units.zh: 以齡之受委大藩，贓罪狼籍，原情取事，死有餘辜。
units.en: Lingzhi had been entrusted with a great frontier post and his bribery was notorious; judged on the facts, death would not exceed his guilt.
units.literal: Considering that Lingzhi was entrusted with a great frontier post and his bribery crimes are notorious, weighing the facts of the case, death would not exceed his guilt.

units.zh: 然既遣詳議，終須近法。
units.en: Yet since the case was sent for full deliberation, the law must finally be followed.
units.literal: Yet since detailed deliberation has already been ordered, in the end the law must be followed.

units.zh: 竊惟議事群官，未盡識議刑本意。
units.en: I fear the assembled officials do not fully understand the original intent of deliberative punishment.
units.literal: Your servant privately considers that the assembled officials do not fully understand the original intent of deliberative punishment.

units.zh: 律有八議，並依《周禮》舊文，矜其異於眾臣，所以特製議法。
units.en: The code provides the Eight Deliberations, following the old text of the Rites of Zhou, to show regard for those who differ from ordinary ministers; that is why deliberative law was specially instituted.
units.literal: The code has the Eight Deliberations, all following the old text of the Rites of Zhou, showing regard for those who differ from ordinary ministers; therefore special deliberative law was instituted.

units.zh: 禮：王族刑於隱者，所以議親；
units.en: The Rites say royal kin are punished in private—that is deliberation for kinship;
units.literal: The Rites say: royal kin are punished in private—therefore deliberation for kinship;

units.zh: 刑不上大夫，所以議貴。
units.en: punishment does not reach great officers—that is deliberation for nobility.
units.literal: punishment does not reach great officers—therefore deliberation for nobility.

units.zh: 知重其親貴，議欲緩刑，非為嫉其賢能，謀致深法。
units.en: Because kin and nobility are esteemed, deliberation seeks to ease punishment—not to envy talent, nor to contrive harsher penalties.
units.literal: Knowing that kin and nobility are esteemed, deliberation seeks to ease punishment; it is not to envy their talent and ability, nor to contrive deep punishment.

units.zh: 今既許議，而加重刑，是與堯、舜相反，不可為萬代法。
units.en: Now that deliberation has been permitted, yet heavier punishment is added—this is contrary to Yao and Shun and cannot be law for ten thousand generations.
units.literal: Now that deliberation has been permitted, yet heavier punishment is added—this is contrary to Yao and Shun and cannot be law for ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 高宗從其奏，齡之竟得流於嶺外。
units.en: Gaozong accepted his argument, and Lingzhi was exiled to the far south instead.
units.literal: Gaozong followed his memorial, and Lingzhi in the end was banished beyond the Lingnan.

units.zh: 尋遷刑部尚書，加金紫光祿大夫，復曆兵部、度支、吏部三尚書，
units.en: He was soon made Minister of Punishments with the Gold-Purple Glory title, and later held the ministries of War, Revenue, and Personnel in turn.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to Minister of Punishments, with the added title Gold-Purple Glory Grand Master, and again served in succession as Minister of War, of Revenue, and of Personnel,

units.zh: 顯慶四年，坐事，貶為潮州刺史。
units.en: In the fourth year of Xianqing, implicated in a case, he was demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xianqing, for an offense he was demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou.

units.zh: 卒官，年六十。
units.en: He died in that post at the age of sixty.
units.literal: He died in office at age sixty.

units.zh: 所撰《冥報記》二卷，大行於世。
units.en: His two-scroll Records of Netherworld Retribution circulated widely.
units.literal: What he compiled, Records of Retribution in the Netherworld in two scrolls, circulated widely in the world.

units.zh: 兄皎，武德初為秦府記室，從太宗征討，專掌書檄，深見親待。
units.en: His elder brother Jiao entered service in the Prince of Qin's secretariat in Wude, followed Taizong on campaign as chief draftsman, and won deep favor.
units.literal: His elder brother Jiao, early in Wude served as Recorder of the Prince of Qin's household; he followed Taizong on campaigns, exclusively managing documents and proclamations, and was deeply favored.

units.zh: 貞觀中，累轉吏部侍郎。
units.en: Under Zhenguan he rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 先是，選集無限，隨到補職，時漸太平，選人稍眾，皎始請以冬初一時大集，終季春而畢，至今行之。
units.en: Earlier, civil-service selections had no fixed season and posts were filled as candidates arrived. As peace returned and candidates multiplied, Jiao proposed a single winter-to-spring selection cycle, a practice that continues today.
units.literal: Previously, selection assemblies had no limit and appointees were filled as they arrived; as the times gradually became peaceful the candidates grew somewhat numerous, and Jiao first requested that a great assembly be held in early winter and concluded by the end of spring—this is practiced to the present.

units.zh: 曆遷益州長史。
units.en: He later served as Administrator of Yizhou.
units.literal: He served in succession as Long Governor of Yizhou.

units.zh: 卒，贈太常卿。
units.en: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously given Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 子之奇，調露中為給事中，坐嚐為章懷太子僚屬徙邊，
units.en: His son Zhiqi was a drafting attendant in the Tiaolu era; for having served Crown Prince Zhanghuai he was exiled.
units.literal: His son Zhiqi, in the Tiaolu era served as Drafting Attendant, and because he had once been an aide to Crown Prince Zhanghuai was banished to the frontier,

units.zh: 文明元年，起為括蒼令，與徐敬業作亂伏誅。
units.en: In the first year of Wenming, Recalled as magistrate of Kuo'ang, he joined Xu Jingye's revolt and was put to death.
units.literal: In the first year of Wenming, he was recalled to serve as Magistrate of Kuo'ang; he joined Xu Jingye's rebellion and was executed.

units.zh: 臨孫紹，博學，善《三禮》。
units.en: Lin's grandson Shao was learned and expert in the Three Rites.
units.literal: Lin's grandson Shao was erudite and skilled in the Three Rites.

units.zh: 神龍中為太常博士，
units.en: During the Shenlong era he served as Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: In the Shenlong era he was Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices,

units.zh: 景龍二年，韋庶人上言：“自妃、主及命婦、宮官，葬日請給鼓吹。”
units.en: In the second year of Jinglong, Empress Wei petitioned that consorts, princesses, titled ladies, and palace women be granted martial music at their funerals.
units.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, the Deposed Empress Wei submitted a memorial: "From consorts and princesses down to titled ladies and palace officers, on burial days request that martial music be granted.

units.zh: 中宗特製許之。
units.en: Emperor Zhongzong specially approved it.
units.literal: Zhongzong by special edict permitted it.

units.zh: 紹上疏諫曰：“竊聞鼓吹之樂，本為軍容。
units.en: Shao remonstrated: "Martial pipe-and-drum music was created for armies.
units.literal: Shao submitted a remonstrance, saying: "I have heard that the music of martial pipes and drums was originally for military array.

units.zh: 昔黃帝涿鹿有功，以為警衛。
units.en: The Yellow Emperor instituted it as a guard of honor after Zhuolu.
units.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor, for merit at Zhuolu, made it a guard of honor.

units.zh: 故棡鼓曲有《靈夔吼》、《雕鶚爭》、《石墜崖》、《壯士怒》之類，自昔功臣備禮，適得用之。
units.en: Its drum pieces—Spirit Kui Roars, Eagle and Goshawk Contend, Stone Falls from the Cliff, Hero's Wrath—were reserved for meritorious ministers.
units.literal: Therefore the rattle-drum tunes have such titles as Spirit Kui Roars, Eagle and Goshawk Contend, Stone Falls from the Cliff, and Hero's Wrath; from old meritorious ministers received full ritual and only then might use it.

units.zh: 丈夫有四方之功，以恩加寵錫。
units.en: Men who won the realm received such honors by imperial grace.
units.literal: A man with merit in the four directions received favor and bestowal of gifts by grace.

units.zh: 假如郊天祀地，誠是重儀，惟有宮懸，本無案據。
units.en: Even at the greatest sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, only the palace bells are prescribed—no precedent for martial music there.
units.literal: Suppose sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—truly this is a weighty rite; only the palace suspended bells exist, and originally there is no precedent for the other.

units.zh: 故知軍樂所備，尚不洽於神祇；
units.en: Military music does not even belong at rites for the gods;
units.literal: Thus one knows that what military music prepares still does not extend to the spirits;

units.zh: 鉦鼓之音，豈能接於閨閫。
units.en: how could gongs and drums enter the women's quarters?
units.literal: how could the sound of bells and drums be joined to inner chambers?

units.zh: 準式，公主、王妃已下葬禮，惟有團扇、方扇、彩帷、錦鄣之色。
units.en: Regulations for princesses and consorts allow only fans, canopies, and brocade screens at burial.
units.literal: By regulation, for burial rites of princesses and imperial consorts and below, there are only round fans, square fans, colored canopies, and brocade screens.

units.zh: 加之鼓吹，曆代未聞。
units.en: Adding martial music has no precedent in any dynasty.
units.literal: Adding martial music—no age has heard of it.

units.zh: 又準令，五品官婚葬，元無鼓吹，惟京官五品，得借四品鼓吹為儀。
units.en: Statute gives fifth-rank officials no martial music at all; only metropolitan fifth-rank officials may borrow fourth-rank music.
units.literal: Moreover by regulation, for fifth-rank officials' weddings and funerals there originally was no martial music; only capital officials of fifth rank might borrow fourth-rank martial music as ceremony.

units.zh: 令特給五品以上母妻，五品官則不當給限，便是班秩本因夫子，儀飾乃復過之。
units.en: Granting it to fifth-rank mothers and wives while denying fifth-rank officials themselves inverts rank, which derives from husband or son.
units.literal: Now to grant specially to mothers and wives above fifth rank, while fifth-rank officials ought not receive the limit—then rank originally derives from husband and son, yet ceremonial display again surpasses them.

units.zh: 事非倫次，難為定制，參詳義理，不可常行。
units.en: The order is wrong, the rule unworkable, and the rite should not become routine.
units.literal: The matter is not in proper order; it is hard to make a fixed rule; examining the meaning and principle, it cannot be regularly practiced.

units.zh: 請停前敕，各依常典。”
units.en: I ask that the recent edict be revoked and old custom restored."
units.literal: I request to stop the prior edict and each follow the usual canon."

units.zh: 疏奏不納。
units.en: The memorial went unheeded.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

units.zh: 紹尋遷左台侍御史，兼太常博士。
units.en: Shao was soon made Left Censor and still served as ritual erudite.
units.literal: Shao was soon moved to Attending Censor of the Left Terrace, concurrently Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 中宗將親拜南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明等希旨皇后為亞獻，紹與博士蔣欽緒固爭以為不可。
units.en: When Zhongzong prepared to sacrifice at the southern suburb, Zhu Qinming and others flattered Empress Wei as secondary offerer; Shao and Jiang Qinxu protested.
units.literal: Zhongzong was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice in person; the National University Rector Zhu Qinming and others, to please the empress, wished her to be secondary offerer; Shao and Erudite Jiang Qinxu firmly contended that this could not be.

units.zh: 又則天父母二陵各置守戶五百人，武三思及子崇訓墓各置守戶六十人。
units.en: Wu Zetian's parents' tombs each received five hundred guard households; Wu Sansi and his son Chongxun each received sixty.
units.literal: Moreover at the two tombs of Wu Zetian's parents five hundred tomb-guard households were established each; at the tombs of Wu Sansi and his son Chongxun sixty guard households each were established.

units.zh: 以武氏外戚乃與昭陵禮同，三思等復逾親王之製，又上疏切諫。
units.en: Equating Wu kin with Taizong's Zhaoling and outdoing princely rites, Shao remonstrated again.
units.literal: Because the Wu clan as maternal kin were made equal in ritual to Zhaoling, and Sansi and others again exceeded the regulations for imperial princes, he again submitted a sharp remonstrance.

units.zh: 當時雖皆不從，深為議者所美。
units.en: None of it was adopted, but contemporaries admired his stand.
units.literal: Although at the time all were not followed, he was deeply praised by discussants.

units.zh: 睿宗即位，又數陳時政損益，累轉給事中，仍知禮儀事。
units.en: Under Ruizong he repeatedly advised on policy, rose to Drafting Attendant, and still oversaw ritual.
units.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he again several times stated gains and losses of current policy, was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Attendant, and still managed ritual matters.

units.zh: 先天二年冬，今上講武於驪山，紹以修儀注不合旨，坐斬。
units.en: In the second year of Xiantian, that winter the emperor drilled troops at Lishan; Shao's ritual directions displeased him and he was sentenced to death.
units.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, in winter the present emperor held martial exercises at Lishan; Shao, because the revised ritual regulations did not match the intent, was punished with execution.

units.zh: 時今上既怒講武失儀，坐紹於纛下，右金吾將軍李邈遽請宣敕，遂斬之。
units.en: Already angry at the disorderly drill, the emperor had Shao sit beneath the command banner; General Li Miao rushed the edict and he was beheaded.
units.literal: At the time the present emperor was already angry that the drill had been disorderly; he seated Shao beneath the banner; the Right Golden Crow General Li Miao hastily requested proclamation of the edict, and he was beheaded.

units.zh: 時人既痛惜紹，而深咎於邈。
units.en: The court mourned Shao and blamed Li Miao.
units.literal: People of the time both grieved for Shao and deeply blamed Miao.

units.zh: 尋有敕罷邈官，遂擯廢終其身。
units.en: An edict soon stripped Miao of office and he never served again.
units.literal: Soon an edict dismissed Miao from office, and he was cast out and idle to the end of his life.

units.zh: 張文瓘，貝州武城人。
units.en: Zhang Wenjun, a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
units.literal: Zhang Wenjun was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou.

units.zh: 大業末徙家魏州之昌樂。
units.en: Late in the Daye era his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.
units.literal: Late in Daye his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

units.zh: 瓘幼孤，事母兄以孝友聞。
units.en: Orphaned young, he was known for devotion to his mother and elder brother.
units.literal: Wenjun was orphaned young; he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

units.zh: 貞觀初，舉明經，補并州參軍。
units.en: In early Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing exam and became a Bingzhou staff officer.
units.literal: Early in Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Staff Officer of Bingzhou.

units.zh: 時英國公李勣為長史，深禮之。
units.en: Li Ji, Duke of Ying, was then regional commander and treated him with great respect.
units.literal: At the time the Duke of Ying Li Ji was Administrator; he deeply honored him.

units.zh: 累遷水部員外郎。
units.en: He rose to vice director of the Water Bureau.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Water Bureau.

units.zh: 時兄文琮為戶部侍郎，舊制兄弟不許並居台閣，遂出為雲陽令。
units.en: His brother Wenzong was Vice Minister of Revenue; regulations barred brothers from the central secretariat, so Wenjun was posted as magistrate of Yunyang.
units.literal: At the time his elder brother Wenzong was Vice Minister of Revenue; by old regulation brothers were not permitted to hold office together in the Censorate and Secretariat, so he was sent out as Magistrate of Yunyang.

units.zh: 龍朔年，累授東西台舍人、參知政事。
units.en: In Longshuo he became a drafting officer on the Eastern and Western Terrace and joined the council of state.
units.literal: In the Longshuo year he was repeatedly appointed Eastern and Western Terrace Drafting Officer and Participant in Governance.

units.zh: 尋遷東台侍郎、同東西台三品，兼知左史事。
units.en: He soon became Eastern Terrace vice minister with third-rank standing and oversaw the left historiographer.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace, Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Eastern and Western Terrace, and concurrently managed Left Historiographer affairs.

units.zh: 時初造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，又征討四夷，廄馬有萬匹，倉庫漸虛。
units.en: New palaces—Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi—were rising, campaigns against the four quarters continued, ten thousand horses filled the stables, and the treasuries thinned.
units.literal: At the time they were first building the Penglai, Shangyang, and Hebi palaces, and also campaigning against the four barbarians; the stables had ten thousand horses and the granaries gradually emptied.

units.zh: 文瓘因進諫曰：“人力不可不惜，百姓不可不養，養之逸則富以康，使之勞則怨以叛。
units.en: Wenjun remonstrated: "Do not waste labor or neglect the people. Ease makes them prosperous; overwork breeds resentment and revolt.
units.literal: Wenjun therefore submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Human labor must not be unspared; the common people must not be unfed; if fed in ease then they grow rich and healthy, if made to labor then they resent and rebel.

units.zh: 秦皇、漢武，廣事四夷，多造宮室，使士崩瓦解，戶口減半。
units.en: Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi campaigned widely and built endlessly until armies shattered and the population halved.
units.literal: Qin Huang and Han Wu, extensively serving the four barbarians and building many palaces, made knights collapse and disintegrate and household registers halved.

units.zh: 臣聞製化於未亂，保邦於未危，人罔常懷，懷於有仁。
units.en: Order is made before chaos, safety before peril; people cling to whoever shows benevolence.
units.literal: Your servant has heard: establish transformation before disorder, preserve the state before danger; people have no constant hold—they hold to benevolence.

units.zh: 陛下不製於未亂之前，安能救於既危之後？
units.en: If you do not act before disorder, how will you rescue the realm once danger arrives?
units.literal: If Your Majesty does not establish rule before disorder, how can you save after danger has come?

units.zh: 百姓不堪其弊，必構禍難，殷鑒不遠，近在隋朝。
units.en: The people cannot endure such burdens; disaster will follow. The lesson is close—the Sui fell only yesterday.
units.literal: The common people cannot bear these harms and will surely bring calamity; the mirror is not far—near at hand is the Sui dynasty.

units.zh: 臣願稍安撫之，無使生怨。”
units.en: I beg you to soothe them and give no cause for anger."
units.literal: Your servant wishes slightly to soothe them and not let resentment arise."

units.zh: 上深納其言，於是節減廄馬數千匹，賜文瓘繒錦百段，
units.en: The emperor took this to heart, cut thousands of horses from the stables, and gave Wenjun a hundred bolts of brocade.
units.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words; thereupon he reduced the stables by several thousand horses and bestowed on Wenjun a hundred lengths of silk brocade,

units.zh: 咸亨三年，官名復舊，改授黃門侍郎，兼太子左庶子。
units.en: In the third year of Xianheng titles reverted to earlier forms; he became Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and junior tutor to the heir apparent.
units.literal: office names reverted to the old forms; he was reassigned as Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 俄遷大理卿，依舊知政事。
units.en: Soon he was Minister of Justice while still in the council.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to Minister of Justice, still managing government affairs as before.

units.zh: 文瓘至官旬日，決遣疑事四百餘條，無不允當，自是人有抵罪者，皆無怨言。
units.en: Within ten days he resolved more than four hundred doubtful cases to general satisfaction; thereafter convicts ceased to complain.
units.literal: Within ten days of Wenjun reaching office he decided and dispatched more than four hundred doubtful cases, none not fitting and proper; from then on those who incurred guilt had no complaint.

units.zh: 文瓘常有疾，係囚相與齋禱，願其視事。
units.en: When he fell ill, prisoners fasted together and prayed for his return.
units.literal: Wenjun often had illness; prisoners together fasted and prayed, wishing him to attend to business.

units.zh: 當時咸稱其執法平恕，以比戴胄，
units.en: All praised his fair and merciful judgments, comparing him to Dai Zhou.
units.literal: At the time all praised his impartial and lenient enforcement of law, comparing him to Dai Zhou,

units.zh: 上元二年，拜侍中，兼太子賓客。
units.en: In the second year of Shangyuan he was made Attendant-in-Chief and guest of the heir apparent.
units.literal: he was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 大理諸囚聞文瓘改官，一時慟哭，其感人心如此。
units.en: Ministry prisoners, hearing of his promotion, wept together—such was their regard.
units.literal: The prisoners of the Ministry of Justice, hearing Wenjun had changed office, all at once wailed; such was his moving of hearts.

units.zh: 文瓘性嚴正，諸司奏議，多所糾駁，高宗甚委之。
units.en: Stern and upright, he corrected many memorials from other offices; Gaozong relied on him heavily.
units.literal: Wenjun's nature was stern and upright; the various offices' submitted deliberations he many times criticized and rejected; Gaozong greatly relied on him.

units.zh: 或時臥疾在家，朝廷每有大事，上必問諸宰臣曰：“與文瓘議未？”
units.en: When ill at home, on great affairs the emperor asked his chancellors, "Have you consulted Wenjun?"
units.literal: Sometimes lying ill at home, whenever the court had a great matter the emperor would ask the chief ministers: "Have you deliberated with Wenjun?"

units.zh: 奏雲未者，則遣共籌之。
units.en: If they had not, he sent them to confer with him.
units.literal: If the reply was not yet, he would send them to plan together.

units.zh: 奏雲已議者，皆報可從之。
units.en: If they had, he approved their decision.
units.literal: If the reply was already deliberated, all were reported as acceptable to follow.

units.zh: 其後，新羅外叛，高宗將發兵討除。
units.en: Later Silla rebelled abroad, and Gaozong prepared to send troops against them.
units.literal: After this, Silla rebelled externally and Gaozong was about to send troops to punish and eliminate them.

units.zh: 時文瓘疾病在家，乃輿疾請見，奏曰：“比為吐蕃犯邊，兵屯寇境，新羅雖未即順，師不內侵。
units.en: Wenjun was ill at home but had himself carried in to see the emperor. He said, "Tibetans are raiding the frontier and troops are massed there. Silla has not yet submitted, but their armies are not marching inland.
units.literal: At the time Wenjun was ill at home; he had himself carried in illness to request an audience and submitted: "Recently because Tibetans violated the border, troops are stationed on the frontier; although Silla has not yet immediately submitted, their armies do not invade inward.

units.zh: 若東西俱事征討，臣恐百姓不堪其弊。
units.en: If we fight on both fronts at once, the people will not endure the burden.
units.literal: If east and west both undertake campaigns, your servant fears the common people cannot bear the harm.

units.zh: 請息兵修德以安百姓。”
units.en: I beg you to halt the armies and cultivate virtue to give the people peace."
units.literal: I request to cease troops and cultivate virtue to settle the common people."

units.zh: 高宗從之。
units.en: Gaozong agreed.
units.literal: Gaozong followed this.

units.zh: 儀鳳二年卒，年七十三，贈幽州都督，諡曰懿。
units.en: In the second year of Yifeng, he died at seventy-three, was posthumously made governor of Youzhou, and given the posthumous name Yi.
units.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, he died at age seventy-three, was posthumously given Governor of Youzhou, and his posthumous title was Yi.

units.zh: 以其經事孝敬皇帝，特敕陪葬恭陵。
units.en: For having served Emperor Xiaojing, he was specially ordered buried at Gongling.
units.literal: Because he had served the Filial and Respectful Emperor, a special edict ordered him buried with honor at Gongling.

units.zh: 四子：潛、沛、洽、涉。
units.en: He had four sons: Qian, Pei, Qia, and She.
units.literal: Four sons: Qian, Pei, Qia, and She.

units.zh: 中宗時，潛官至魏州刺史，沛同州刺史，洽衛尉卿，涉殿中監。
units.en: Under Zhongzong, Qian became prefect of Wei, Pei of Tong, Qia commandant of the guards, and She director of the palace directorate.
units.literal: In the Zhongzong era, Qian reached Prefect of Weizhou, Pei Tong Prefecture, Qia Commandant of the Guards, and She Director of the Palace.

units.zh: 父子兄弟五人皆至三品官，時人謂之“萬石張家”。
units.en: Father and four sons all reached third rank; contemporaries called them the Zhang family of ten thousand stone.
units.literal: Father, sons, and brothers—five men—all reached third-rank office; people of the time called them the "Wanshi Zhang family."

units.zh: 及韋溫等被誅之際，涉為亂兵所殺。
units.en: When Wei Wen and his faction were killed, She died at the hands of mutinous troops.
units.literal: When Wei Wen and others were executed, She was killed by mutinous soldiers.

units.zh: 兄文琮，貞觀中為持書侍御史。
units.en: His elder brother Wenzong was an attending censor in Zhenguan.
units.literal: His elder brother Wenzong, in Zhenguan served as Attending Censor holding the imperial writing.

units.zh: 三遷毫州刺史，為政清簡，百姓安之。
units.en: Promoted thrice to prefect of Bozhou, he governed plainly and the people were content.
units.literal: Three times moved to Prefect of Bozhou; his governance was clear and simple and the common people were at peace.

units.zh: 永徽初，表獻《太宗文皇帝頌》，優製褒美，賜絹百匹，征拜戶部侍郎。
units.en: In early Yonghui he presented an eulogy to Taizong; the emperor praised it, gave a hundred bolts of silk, and made him Vice Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: Early in Yonghui he submitted a memorial offering Eulogy for Emperor Taizong, Wen; an excellent edict praised him, bestowed a hundred bolts of silk, and summoned him as Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 從母弟房遺愛以罪貶授房州刺史，文琮作詩祖餞。
units.en: His cousin Fang Yiai, convicted, was demoted to Fangzhou; Wenzong wrote a farewell poem.
units.literal: His maternal cousin Fang Yiai, for a crime, was demoted and appointed Prefect of Fangzhou; Wenzong composed a poem to send him off.

units.zh: 及遺愛誅，坐是出為建州刺史。
units.en: When Yiai was executed, Wenzong was posted out as prefect of Jianzhou.
units.literal: When Yiai was executed, for this he was sent out as Prefect of Jianzhou.

units.zh: 州境素尚淫祀，不修社稷。
units.en: The region favored improper cults and neglected the state altars.
units.literal: The prefecture had long favored licentious sacrifices and did not repair the altars of soil and grain.

units.zh: 文琮下教書曰：“春秋二社，蓋本為農，惟獨此州，廢而不立。
units.en: He issued an instruction: "The spring and autumn communal rites exist for farming; this prefecture alone has abandoned them.
units.literal: Wenzong issued an instruction, saying: "The two seasonal communal sacrifices of spring and autumn are fundamentally for agriculture; only this prefecture abolished them and did not establish them.

units.zh: 禮典既闕，風俗何觀？
units.en: With ritual neglected, what custom remains to follow?
units.literal: The ritual canon is already lacking—what is there to model in custom?

units.zh: 近年已來，田多不熟，抑不祭先農所致乎！
units.en: In recent years the fields have often failed—is this not because the god of agriculture goes unhonored?
units.literal: In recent years fields have often not ripened—is this perhaps because the Former Farmer is not sacrificed to!

units.zh: 神在於敬，何以邀福？”
units.en: Spirits respond to reverence, not to bribery."
units.literal: The spirits lie in reverence—how seek blessing?"

units.zh: 於是示其節限條製，百姓欣而行之。
units.en: He then published the seasonal rules, and the people gladly obeyed.
units.literal: Thereupon he displayed the seasonal limits and regulations, and the common people gladly carried them out.

units.zh: 尋卒。
units.en: He soon died.
units.literal: Soon he died.

units.zh: 文集二十卷。
units.en: His collected works ran to twenty scrolls.
units.literal: Collected writings in twenty scrolls.

units.zh: 子戩，官至江州刺史，撰《喪儀纂要》七卷，行於時。
units.en: His son Jian became prefect of Jiangzhou and wrote Essentials of Mourning Rites in seven scrolls, widely used in his day.
units.literal: His son Jian reached Prefect of Jiangzhou and compiled Essentials of Mourning Rites in seven scrolls, current in the age.

units.zh: 戩弟錫，則天時為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。
units.en: Jian's brother Xi under Wu Zetian was vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and chancellor.
units.literal: Jian's younger brother Xi, in Wu Zetian's time was Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Tower.

units.zh: 先是，姊子李嶠知政事，錫拜官，而嶠罷相出為國子祭酒，舅甥相代為相，時人榮之。
units.en: Earlier his nephew Li Qiao had been chancellor; when Xi was appointed, Qiao left office as rector of the National University—uncle and nephew succeeding each other as chief ministers, to the admiration of the age.
units.literal: Previously his sister's son Li Qiao managed government affairs; when Xi received appointment, Qiao ceased being chancellor and went out as Rector of the National University—maternal uncle and nephew succeeding each other as chancellor; people of the time honored this.

units.zh: 錫與鄭杲俱知天官選事，坐贓，則天將斬之以徇，臨刑而特赦之。
units.en: Xi and Zheng Gao oversaw personnel selection; convicted of bribery, they were about to be executed when Wu Zetian pardoned them at the block.
units.literal: Xi together with Zheng Gao both managed Celestial Office selection affairs; for bribery Wu Zetian was about to behead them as a warning, but at execution they received special pardon.

units.zh: 中宗時，累遷工部尚書，兼修國史，尋令於東都留守。
units.en: Under Zhongzong he rose to Minister of Works, helped revise the national history, and was left to guard the eastern capital.
units.literal: In the Zhongzong era he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently revised the national history, and soon was ordered to remain at the eastern capital.

units.zh: 中宗崩，韋庶人臨朝，詔錫與刑部尚書裴談並同中書門下三品。
units.en: After Zhongzong's death Empress Wei ruled; Xi and Pei Tan were made chancellors of the third rank.
units.literal: When Zhongzong died, the Deposed Empress Wei held court; an edict made Xi and Minister of Punishments Pei Tan both Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 旬日，出為絳州刺史。
units.en: Ten days later he was posted as prefect of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Within ten days he was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 累封平原郡公，以年老致仕而卒。
units.en: Enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan, he retired for age and died.
units.literal: Repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan, he retired for old age and died.

units.zh: 文琮從父弟文收，隋內史舍人虔威子也。
units.en: Wenzong's cousin Wenshou was the son of the Sui interior secretary Qianwei.
units.literal: Wenzong's paternal cousin Wenshou was son of Sui Interior Secretary Attendant Qianwei.

units.zh: 尤善音律，嚐覽蕭吉《樂譜》，以為未甚詳悉，更博采群言及曆代沿革，裁竹為十二律吹之，備盡旋宮之義。
units.en: Skilled in music theory, he found Xiao Ji's treatise incomplete, studied wider sources, cut bamboo pipes for the twelve pitches, and demonstrated full cyclical modulation.
units.literal: He was especially skilled in pitch and mode; once he perused Xiao Ji's Music Treatise and thought it not very detailed, and further broadly gathered many statements and successive ages' changes and reforms, cut bamboo for the twelve modes and blew them, fully completing the meaning of cyclical modes.

units.zh: 時太宗將創製禮樂，召文收於太常，令與少卿祖孝孫參定雅樂。
units.en: When Taizong was creating court music, Wenshou was called to the Imperial Sacrifices office to work with Zu Xiaosun.
units.literal: At the time Taizong was about to create ritual music; he summoned Wenshou to the Imperial Sacrifices office and ordered him with Vice Director Zu Xiaosun to fix the elegant music.

units.zh: 太樂有古鍾十二，近代惟用其七，餘有五，俗號啞鍾，莫能通者。
units.en: The court had twelve ancient bells; only seven were used in recent times—the other five, called mute bells, could not be sounded.
units.literal: The Grand Music had twelve ancient bells; in recent times only seven were used; the remaining five, commonly called mute bells, none could make sound.

units.zh: 文收吹律調之，聲皆響徹，時人咸服其妙。
units.en: Wenshou tuned them with his pipes until all rang clear, to general admiration.
units.literal: Wenshou blew modes to tune them; all sounds rang clear; people of the time all submitted to his subtlety.

units.zh: 尋授協律郎。
units.en: He was soon made harmonizing officer.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Harmonizing Officer.

units.zh: 十一年，文收表請厘正太樂，上謂侍臣曰：“樂本緣人，人和則樂和。
units.en: In year eleven he asked to reform court music; the emperor told his ministers, "Music follows the people—when people are at peace, music is in harmony.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Wenshou memorialized requesting to rectify Grand Music; the emperor told attendant officials: "Music fundamentally follows people; if people are harmonious then music is harmonious.

units.zh: 至如隋煬帝末年，天下喪亂，縱令改張音律，知其終不和諧。
units.en: At the end of Sui Yangdi's reign the realm was in chaos; even if you changed the pitches, they would not harmonize.
units.literal: As for late in Sui Yangdi's reign, the realm was in disorder and mourning; even if one changed and spread pitch and mode, one knows in the end it would not be harmonious.

units.zh: 若使四海無事，百姓安樂，音律自然調和，不藉更改。”
units.en: When the realm is tranquil and the people content, music harmonizes of itself without reform."
units.literal: If the four seas had no affairs and the common people were at ease and happy, pitch and mode would naturally be harmonious without relying on change."

units.zh: 竟不依其請。
units.en: His request was denied.
units.literal: In the end he did not follow his request.

units.zh: 十四年，景雲見，河水清，文收采《朱雁天馬》之義，製《景雲河清》樂，名曰“燕樂”，奏之管弦，為樂之首，今元會第一奏者是也，
units.en: In year fourteen, when auspicious clouds and a clear Yellow River appeared, he composed "Auspicious Clouds and Clear River," called Yan Music—the piece still opened the New Year court.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, auspicious clouds appeared and the Yellow River ran clear; Wenshou took the meaning of Vermilion Goose and Heavenly Horse and composed the music "Auspicious Clouds and Clear River," named "Yan Music"; played on pipes and strings, it was first among music—what is now first played at the New Year assembly is this,

units.zh: 咸亨元年，遷太子率更令，卒官。
units.en: In the first year of Xianheng, He was then made rate master of the heir apparent and died in office.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, he was moved to Rate Master of the Heir Apparent and died in office.

units.zh: 撰《新樂書》十二卷。
units.en: He wrote New Music Book in twelve scrolls.
units.literal: He compiled New Music Book in twelve scrolls.

units.zh: 徐有功，國子博士文遠孫也。
units.en: Xu Yougong, grandson of National University erudite Xu Wenyuan.
units.literal: Xu Yougong was grandson of Erudite of the National University Xu Wenyuan.

units.zh: 舉明經，累轉蒲州司法參軍，紹封東莞男。
units.en: He passed the Mingjing exam, served as judicial officer in Puzhou, and inherited the barony of Dongguan.
units.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly promoted to Judicial Staff Officer of Puzhou, inheriting the enfeoffment Baron of Dongguan.

units.zh: 為政寬仁，不行杖罰。
units.en: He governed with leniency and never used the beating staff.
units.literal: In governing he was lenient and benevolent and did not apply the staff penalty.

units.zh: 吏人感其恩信，遞相約曰：“若犯徐司法杖者，眾必斥罰之。”
units.en: Officials and people, trusting him, agreed among themselves that anyone who forced Xu to use the staff would be shamed by the community.
units.literal: Officials and people were moved by his grace and trust and in turn agreed: "If anyone violates Staff Officer Xu's staff, the multitude will surely reprove and punish him."

units.zh: 由是人爭用命，終於代滿，不戮一人，
units.en: They competed to obey the law, and when his term ended not a single person had been executed.
units.literal: Therefore people vied to fulfill orders; by the end of his term of replacement not one was put to death,

units.zh: 載初元年，累遷司刑丞。
units.en: In the first year of Zaichu, He was then promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
units.literal: In the first year of Zaichu, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Punishments.

units.zh: 時酷吏周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、王弘義等構陷無辜，皆抵極法，公卿震恐，莫敢正言。
units.en: Cruel officials such as Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and Wang Hongyi framed the innocent to extreme punishments while the court fell silent.
units.literal: At the time the cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi, and others framed the innocent; all reached extreme law; dukes and ministers trembled in fear and none dared speak straight.

units.zh: 有功獨存平恕，詔下大理者，有功皆議出之，前後濟活數十百家。
units.en: Yougong alone remained fair and lenient; cases sent to the Grand Court he argued to release, saving dozens of families.
units.literal: Yougong alone preserved fairness and leniency; those sent down to the Grand Court by edict Yougong all deliberated to release; before and after he saved several tens of families.

units.zh: 常於殿庭論奏曲直，則天厲色詰之，左右莫不悚栗，有功神色不撓，爭之彌切。
units.en: He often argued cases in court; Wu Zetian questioned him angrily while attendants trembled, but he did not flinch and argued all the harder.
units.literal: He often in the palace hall debated right and wrong in cases; Wu Zetian with stern countenance interrogated him; those left and right were all fearful, yet Yougong's expression did not bend and he contended all the more keenly.

units.zh: 尋轉秋官員外郎，轉郎中。
units.en: He soon became vice director and then director of the Autumn Office.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Director of the Autumn Office, then Director.

units.zh: 俄而鳳閣侍郎任知古、冬官尚書裴行本等七人被構陷當死，則天謂公卿曰：“古人以殺止殺，我今以恩止殺。
units.en: Soon Ren Zhigu, Pei Xingben, and five others were framed for death; Wu Zetian told the court, "The ancients stopped killing by killing; I stop killing by grace.
units.literal: Soon Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Ren Zhigu, Winter Office Minister Pei Xingben, and seven others were framed and should die; Wu Zetian told the dukes and ministers: "The ancients used killing to stop killing; I now use grace to stop killing.

units.zh: 就群公乞知古等，賜以再生，各授以官，佇申來效。”
units.en: I ask you to spare Zhigu and the rest, give them office, and await their service."
units.literal: I approach the assembled lords to beg Zhigu and the others, grant them renewed life, each confer office, and wait to declare future merit."

units.zh: 俊臣、張知默等又抗表請申大法，則天不許之。
units.en: Lai Junchen and Zhang Zhimou protested for harsh law, but she refused.
units.literal: Junchen, Zhang Zhimou, and others again submitted memorials requesting application of the great law; Wu Zetian did not permit it.

units.zh: 俊臣乃獨引行本，重驗前罪，奏曰：“行本潛行悖逆，告張知蹇與廬陵王反不實，罪當處斬。”
units.en: Junchen alone brought Xingben back, re-examined the case, and said Xingben had falsely reported the Prince of Luling's rebellion and deserved death.
units.literal: Junchen then alone led out Xingben, again verified the former crime, and submitted: "Xingben secretly acted in rebellion, reporting to Zhang Zhijian that the Prince of Luling's rebellion was untrue—the crime should be execution."

units.zh: 有功駁奏曰：“俊臣乖明主再生之賜，虧聖人恩信之道。
units.en: Yougong rebutted: "Junchen defies your gift of life and betrays imperial grace.
units.literal: Yougong rebutted the memorial, saying: "Junchen violates the enlightened ruler's gift of renewed life and damages the sage's path of grace and trust.

units.zh: 為臣雖當嫉惡，然事君必將順其美。”
units.en: A minister must hate evil, yet serve the ruler by following his good intent."
units.literal: As a minister one must hate evil, yet in serving the ruler one must follow his excellence.

units.zh: 行本竟以免死。
units.en: Xingben was spared after all.
units.literal: Xingben in the end was spared death.

units.zh: 道州刺史李仁褒及弟榆次令長沙，又為唐奉一所構，高宗末私議吉凶，謀復李氏，將誅之。
units.en: Li Renbao, prefect of Dao, and his younger brother Changsha, magistrate of Yuci, were framed by Tang Fengyi for private divination plotting to restore the Li house.
units.literal: Dao Prefecture Inspector Li Renbao and his younger brother, Magistrate of Yuci Changsha, were again framed by Tang Fengyi; at the end of Gaozong they privately discussed fortune and misfortune, plotting to restore the Li clan, and were about to be executed.

units.zh: 有功又固爭之，不能得。
units.en: Yougong argued fiercely but could not save them.
units.literal: Yougong again firmly contended but could not succeed.

units.zh: 秋官侍郎周興奏有功曰：“臣聞兩漢故事，附下罔上者腰斬，麵欺者亦斬。
units.en: Zhou Xing memorialized against Yougong, saying, "I have heard that in Han precedents, those who fawn on subordinates and deceive superiors are cut at the waist.
units.literal: Autumn Office Vice Minister Zhou Xing memorialized against Yougong, saying: "Your servant has heard that in the two Han stories, those who fawn on subordinates and deceive superiors are cut at the waist, and those who deceive to the face are also beheaded.

units.zh: 又《禮》云：析言破律者殺。
units.en: The Rites also say those who twist words to break the law are killed.
units.literal: Moreover the Rites say: those who analyze words to break statutes are killed.

units.zh: 有功故出反囚，罪當不赦，請推按其罪。”
units.en: Yougong released rebels and should not be forgiven; investigate him."
units.literal: Yougong deliberately released rebel prisoners—the crime should not be pardoned; I request investigation and prosecution of his crime."

units.zh: 則天雖不許係問，然竟坐免官。
units.en: She did not imprison him but removed him from office.
units.literal: Although Wu Zetian did not permit binding and interrogation, in the end he sat and was removed from office.

units.zh: 久之，起為左台侍御史，則天特褒異之。
units.en: After a time he was restored as left censor, which Wu Zetian specially praised.
units.literal: After a long time he was raised as Attending Censor of the Left Terrace; Wu Zetian especially praised and distinguished him.

units.zh: 時遠近聞有功授職，皆欣然相賀。
units.en: Near and far rejoiced at his appointment.
units.literal: At the time near and far, hearing Yougong received appointment, all gladly congratulated one another.

units.zh: 有功嚐上疏論天官、秋官及朝堂三司理匭使愆失，其略曰：“陛下即位已來，海內職員一定，而天下選人漸多。
units.en: Yougong once memorialized on abuses in personnel, punishments, and the accusation offices, saying, "Since Your Majesty took the throne, offices within the realm have been fixed, yet candidates throughout the land have steadily increased.
units.literal: Yougong once submitted a memorial discussing faults of the Celestial Office, Autumn Office, and the court's Three Offices for managing the accusation box; the summary said: "Since Your Majesty took the throne, offices within the seas are fixed, yet candidates throughout the realm gradually increase.

units.zh: 掌選之曹用舍不平，補擬乖次，囑請公行，顏麵罔懼。
units.en: Selection offices were partial, appointments disorderly, patronage brazen, and faces shameless.
units.literal: The offices managing selection use appointment and dismissal unfairly, supplementation and assignment out of order, patronage requests run openly, and faces show no fear.

units.zh: 遂使囂謗滿路，怨讟盈朝，浸以為常，殊無愧憚。
units.en: Slander filled the roads and resentment the court, treated as normal without shame.
units.literal: Thus clamor and slander fill the roads and resentment overflows the court, gradually becoming normal, especially without shame or dread.

units.zh: 又往屬唐朝季年，時多逆節，鞫訊結斷，刑獄至嚴。
units.en: In late Tang times rebellions multiplied and punishments were severe.
units.literal: Moreover in former years at the Tang dynasty's end, the time had many rebellious acts; inquisition and judgment concluded, and penal prisons were extremely severe.

units.zh: 革命以來，載祀遽積，餘風未殄，用法猶深。
units.en: Since the Zhou revolution old harsh ways lingered.
units.literal: Since the revolution, years have swiftly accumulated; residual winds are not exhausted and application of law is still deep.

units.zh: 今推鞫者猶行酷法，妄劾斷。
units.en: Inquisitors still used cruel methods and false impeachments.
units.literal: Now those who push inquisition still practice cruel law and falsely impeach and judge.

units.zh: 臣即按驗，奏而劾之，獲其枉狀，請即付法斷罪，亦奪祿貶考，以慚其德。
units.en: He would investigate, impeach, punish, and strip rank from offenders.
units.literal: Your servant will then investigate and verify, memorialize and impeach; obtain their wrongful situation, request immediate delivery to law for judgment of crime, also strip salary and degrade evaluation, to shame their virtue.

units.zh: 其三司受表及理匭申冤使，不速與奪，致令擁塞，有理不為申者，亦望準前彈奏，貶考奪祿。
units.en: He asked the same for slow grievance offices and obstruction of just appeals.
units.literal: The Three Offices receiving memorials and the accusation-box grievance envoys, not swiftly deciding, cause blockage to pile up; where there is reason but no appeal is made, I also hope to follow the former impeachment, degrade evaluation and strip salary.

units.zh: 臣昔處法司，緣蒙擢用，臣無以上答至造，願以執法酬恩。
units.en: Having risen through the law offices, he wished to repay favor by strict but fair enforcement.
units.literal: Your servant formerly was in the law office and by grace received promotion; your servant has nothing above to repay supreme creation and wishes to repay grace by enforcing law.

units.zh: 無縱詭隨，不避強禦，猛噬鷙擊，是臣之分。
units.en: He would not indulge guile or avoid the powerful—that was his duty.
units.literal: Do not indulge guile and compliance, do not avoid the strong and overbearing—fierce biting and fierce striking is your servant's portion.

units.zh: 如蒙允納，請降敕施行，庶不越旬時，亦可以除殘革弊，刑措不用，天下幸甚。”
units.en: If approved, he asked an edict so that within ten days abuses might end and punishments fall unused—the realm's great fortune."
units.literal: If I receive permission to accept, I request to descend an edict for implementation; perhaps within no more than ten days, one may also eliminate the cruel and reform abuses, punishments set aside unused—the realm would be greatly fortunate.

units.zh: 後潤州刺史竇孝諶妻龐氏為奴誣告，雲夜解祈福，則天令給事中薛季昶鞫之。
units.en: Later Lady Pang, wife of Run prefect Dou Xiaochen, was accused by a slave of illicit night prayers; Wu Zetian sent Xue Jichang to investigate.
units.literal: Later the wife of Run Prefecture Inspector Dou Xiaochen, Lady Pang, was slandered by a slave, saying she untied her hair at night to pray for blessing; Wu Zetian ordered Drafting Attendant Xue Jichang to interrogate.

units.zh: 季昶鍛練成其罪，龐氏當坐斬。
units.en: Jichang tortured a confession; she was sentenced to death.
units.literal: Jichang forged and refined until the crime was complete; Lady Pang should sit beheading.

units.zh: 有功獨明其無罪。
units.en: Yougong alone proved her innocent.
units.literal: Yougong alone clarified that she had no crime.

units.zh: 而季昶等返陷有功黨援惡逆，奏付法，法司結刑當棄市。
units.en: Jichang then framed Yougong as aiding traitors; the law office sentenced him to public execution.
units.literal: But Jichang and others in return framed Yougong as party to aiding the wicked and rebellious, memorialized for delivery to law; the law office concluded punishment as abandonment in the market.

units.zh: 有功方視事，令史垂泣以告，有功曰：“豈吾獨死，而諸人長不死耶？”
units.en: While at his desk, clerks wept to tell him; he said, "Am I the only man who dies while others live forever?"
units.literal: Yougong was just attending to business; the clerks wept to inform him; Yougong said: "Could it be that I alone die while all others long do not die?"

units.zh: 乃徐起而歸。
units.en: Then he rose calmly and went home.
units.literal: Then he slowly rose and returned home.

units.zh: 則天覽奏，召有功詰之曰：“卿比斷獄，失出何多？”
units.en: Wu Zetian summoned him and said, "Your judgments release too many criminals."
units.literal: Wu Zetian read the memorial and summoned Yougong to interrogate him, saying: "You compared to judging cases—releases mistaken, how many?"

units.zh: 對曰：“失出，臣下之小過；
units.en: He replied, "Mistaken release is a small fault of ministers;
units.literal: He replied: "Mistaken release is a small fault of ministers;

units.zh: 好生，聖人之大德。
units.en: cherishing life is the sage's great virtue.
units.literal: cherishing life is the great virtue of sages.

units.zh: 願陛下弘大德，則天下幸甚。”
units.en: If Your Majesty expands great virtue, the realm will be fortunate."
units.literal: I wish Your Majesty to expand great virtue—then the realm would be greatly fortunate.

units.zh: 則天默然。
units.en: She was silent.
units.literal: Wu Zetian was silent.

units.zh: 於是龐氏減死，流於嶺表，有功除名為庶人。
units.en: Lady Pang's sentence was reduced to exile; Yougong was reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: Thereupon Lady Pang's death was reduced; she was banished beyond the Lingnan frontier; Yougong was removed from name and made commoner.

units.zh: 尋起為左司郎中，累遷司刑少卿。
units.en: Soon he was restored as director of the left department and rose to vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: Soon he was raised as Director of the Left Department, repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 有功謂所親曰：“今身為大理，人命所懸，必不能順旨詭辭以求苟免。”
units.en: He told his friends, "As Grand Justice I hold lives in my hands; I cannot twist words to save myself."
units.literal: Yougong told those close to him: "Now my person is Grand Justice; human lives hang in the balance—I surely cannot follow intent with guileful words to seek careless escape."

units.zh: 故前後為獄官，以諫奏枉誅者，三經斷死，而執誌不渝，酷吏由是少衰，時人比漢之於、張焉。
units.en: As a prison official he three times faced death sentences for defending the wronged, yet did not bend; cruel officials somewhat faded; men compared him to Yu and Zhang of Han.
units.literal: Therefore before and after as prison official, with remonstrance memorials on wrongful executions, three times he passed death judgment yet his purpose did not change; cruel officials thereby somewhat declined; people of the time compared him to Han's Yu and Zhang.

units.zh: 或曰：“若獄官皆然，刑措何遠。”
units.en: Some said that if all judges were like him, punishments would fall unused.
units.literal: Some said: "If all prison officials were thus, punishments set aside—how far off?"

units.zh: 久之，轉司仆少卿。
units.en: After a time he became vice minister of the imperial carriage office.
units.literal: After a long time he was moved to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Carriage.

units.zh: 長安二年卒，年六十二，贈司刑卿。
units.en: In the second year of Chang'an, he died at sixty-two and was posthumously made vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, he died at age sixty-two, posthumously given Vice Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 中宗即位，製曰：“忠正之臣，自昔攸尚；
units.en: When Zhongzong succeeded, an edict said, "Loyal ministers have always been honored;
units.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, an edict said: "Loyal and upright ministers have from old been honored;

units.zh: 褒贈之典，舊章所重。
units.en: Honoring the dead with praise and gifts was always esteemed in precedent.
units.literal: The canon of praise and posthumous gift is what old regulations esteem.

units.zh: 故贈大理卿徐有功，節操貞勁，器懷亮直，徇古人之誌業，實一代之賢良，司彼刑書，深存敬慎。
units.en: The late Grand Justice Xu Yougong was firm in integrity, bright and upright in character, devoted to the ancients' ideals, a true worthy of his age who handled the penal codes with deep reverent care.
units.literal: Therefore the posthumously given Grand Justice Xu Yougong, whose integrity was firm and strong and whose capacity embraced brightness and uprightness, followed the ancients' aims and work, truly a worthy of his generation; he managed those penal writings and deeply preserved reverent caution.

units.zh: 周興、來俊臣等性惟殘酷，務在誅夷，不順其情，立加誣害。
units.en: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their ilk were cruel by nature, bent on slaughter, and would fabricate charges without regard to truth.
units.literal: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others by nature were only cruel; they strove to exterminate and slay; not following the facts, they immediately added false harm.

units.zh: 有功卓然守法，雖死不移，無屈撓之心，有忠烈之議。
units.en: Yougong stood out in upholding the law, unshaken even before death, never yielding, and spoke with loyal fierceness.
units.literal: Yougong outstandingly upheld law; though death he did not shift; he had no heart of bending or yielding and had loyal and fierce deliberation.

units.zh: 當其執斷，並遇平反，定國、釋之，何以加此。
units.en: In his judgments he repeatedly secured reversals of wrongful convictions—what more could Ding Guo or Shi Zhi have added?
units.literal: When he held judgment and decided, all met reversal of wrongful cases; how could Ding Guo and Shi Zhi surpass this?

units.zh: 朕惟新庶政，追想前跡，其人既歿，其德可稱。
units.en: As I renew the government, I recall his path: though he is gone, his virtue deserves praise.
units.literal: We alone renew the multitude of policies, recall former traces; the man has already died, yet his virtue can be praised.

units.zh: 追往贈終，慰茲泉壤。
units.en: Let posthumous honors comfort him in the grave.
units.literal: Pursue the past and gift the end, comfort these springs and soil.

units.zh: 可贈越州刺史，仍遣使就家吊祭，賜物百段，授一子官。”
units.en: Let him be posthumously made prefect of Yuezhou; send envoys to mourn at his home, grant a hundred gifts, and give office to one son."
units.literal: He may be posthumously given Prefect of Yuezhou; still send envoys to his home to mourn and sacrifice, bestow a hundred items, and confer office on one son."

units.zh: 今上踐祚，竇孝諶之子希瑊等請以身之官爵讓有功子惀，以報舊恩。
units.en: When the present emperor succeeded, Dou Xiaochen's son Xizhen and others asked to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of old kindness.
units.literal: When the present emperor trod the throne, Dou Xiaochen's son Xizhen and others requested to yield their own offices and ranks to Yougong's son Lun, to repay old grace.

units.zh: 惀由是自太子司議郎、恭陵令累遷申王府司馬，卒。
units.en: Lun rose from admonisher to the crown prince and magistrate of Gongling to major of the Prince of Shen's household, and died.
units.literal: Lun from this was from Crown Prince Admonishing Attendant, Magistrate of Gongling, repeatedly promoted to Prince of Shen's Household Major, and died.

units.zh: 【論贊】史臣曰：文法，理具之大者，故舜命皋陶為士，昌言誡敕，勤亦至焉。
units.en: [Discussion] The historian writes: Penal law is among the great instruments of governance; Shun appointed Gao Yao minister of crime and exhorted him with clear admonitions—such was the diligence required.
units.literal: [Discussion and Praise] The historiographer says: Literary law is among the great instruments of principle; therefore Shun appointed Gao Yao as minister of crime, and with bright words admonished and instructed—diligence also reached there.

units.zh: 蓋人命所懸，一失其平，冤不可復，聖王所以疚心也。
units.en: Human lives hang in the balance; one lapse from fairness leaves injustice beyond repair—this is why sage rulers grieve.
units.literal: For human lives hang upon it; once balance is lost, injustice cannot be restored—the sage king therefore is pained in heart.

units.zh: 如臨之守法，文瓘之議刑，時屬哲王，可以理奪。
units.en: Men such as Lin, who upheld the law, and Wenjun, who weighed punishments, flourished under wise rulers who could be swayed by reason.
units.literal: Such as Lin's upholding law and Wenjun's deliberating punishments—when the time belonged to a wise king, one could prevail by reason.

units.zh: 當賊後遷鼎之際，酷吏羅織之辰，徐有功獨抗群邪，持平不撓，此所以為難也。
units.en: In the age after rebellion and the move of the capital, when cruel officials wove false charges, Xu Yougong alone stood against the wicked and held the scales level—no small feat.
units.literal: At the time after the rebel moved the tripod, in the hour when cruel officials wove nets, Xu Yougong alone resisted the multitude of evil, held balance and did not bend—this is why it was difficult.

units.zh: 比釋之、定國，徐又過之。
units.en: Beside Shi Zhi and Ding Guo, Xu Yougong was greater still.
units.literal: Compared to Shi Zhi and Ding Guo, Xu again surpassed them.

units.zh: 希瑊讓爵酬恩，可知遺愛。
units.en: Xizhen's yielding of rank to repay kindness shows how deeply he was loved.
units.literal: Xizhen yielded rank to repay grace—one can know the love he left behind.

units.zh: 讚曰：聽訟惟明，持法惟平。
units.en: Praise runs: Hear lawsuits with clarity; hold the law with fairness.
units.literal: The praise says: In hearing lawsuits be only clear; in holding law be only level.

units.zh: 二者或爽，人何以生？
units.en: When either fails, how can the people live?
units.literal: If these two are at times wrong, how can people live?

units.zh: 猗歟徐公，獬豸之精。
units.en: Ah, Lord Xu—you were the spirit of the xiezhi, the beast of justice.
units.literal: Ah, Lord Xu—the essence of the xiezhi.

units.zh: 世皆紛濁，不改吾清。
units.en: Though the world was turbid, he did not change his clarity.
units.literal: The age is all turbid and muddy; he did not change his clarity.
